cards.explanation: The answer is True. The text says the people of Judah and Israel were "…eating and drinking and rejoicing." (1 Kings 4:20) They were as numerous as the sand on the seashore, and the verse says they were rejoicing. That's a party with a guest list I could never bake for, friends.

The answer is False. The text says the kingdoms "…offered tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life." (1 Kings 4:21) Offering tribute and serving is what the verse describes, so rebelling every chance they get doesn't match. I would LOVE for my dough to cooperate like that, friends.

The answer is peace. The text says Solomon "…had peace on all sides." (1 Kings 4:24) He had dominion over all the kingdoms from Tiphsah to Gaza, and peace came with it, friends. Peace on all sides, no matter which way he turned.

The answer is God Himself. The text says "…God gave Solomon wisdom, exceedingly deep insight, and understanding beyond measure…" (1 Kings 4:29) It came as a gift from God, friends. Solomon didn't pick it up at a seminar or find it in a drawer, and believe me, I've checked a few drawers.

The answer is False. The text says "…his fame spread throughout the surrounding nations." (1 Kings 4:31) Solomon's name got out past the border and into other nations, friends. I was famous in exactly one junk drawer, so I'm taking notes.

The answer is that he composes thousands of proverbs and songs. The text says "Solomon composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five." (1 Kings 4:32) That's three thousand proverbs and a thousand and five songs, friends. I once wrote a grocery list and called it a week's work.

The answer is animals and birds and reptiles and fish. The text says "…he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish." (1 Kings 4:33) He spoke of trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing in the wall, and then taught about those creatures too, friends. Trees, animals, birds, reptiles and fish, all in one man's teaching.

The answer is that they send men to listen to him. The text says "…men of all nations came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom." (1 Kings 4:34) Kings sent their own people just to listen, friends. That's a king saying, go sit in on that teaching for me.
